content: SPIKE-02 candidate packages, from api.nuget.org flatcontainer index.json and .nuspec plus registration5 (authoritative registry API; Context7 MCP was not available in the subagent environment and would be weaker than the registry for exact version strings and declared dependency floors). CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Controls.SettingsControls latest STABLE 8.2.251219 published 2025-12-20, latest any 8.3.260402-preview2 published 2026-04-02; owner Microsoft.Toolkit; projectUrl github.com/CommunityToolkit/Windows. 8.2.251219 windows-TFM deps are CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Triggers 8.2.251219 plus Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 1.6.250108002 as a FLOOR (NuGet minimum-version, so 2.3.1 satisfies it with no NU1605). 8.3.260402-preview2 instead depends on the COMPONENT package Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.WinUI 1.8.260204000, which is exactly the MSB4011 dual-family landmine Winhance csproj warns about, so the 8.3 preview train is a trap for a project sitting on the 2.3.1 metapackage. CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Controls.Primitives 8.2.251219 depends on CommunityToolkit.WinUI.Extensions 8.2.251219 plus the same WinAppSDK floor. CommunityToolkit.WinUI.UI.Controls.DataGrid has only 6 versions ever, latest 7.1.2 published 2021-11-18, sole dep Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 1.0.0 and no toolkit coupling, confirming the frozen claim. There is NO 8.x under the CommunityToolkit.WinUI metapackage id; that id also stops at 7.1.2, so 'add CommunityToolkit.WinUI' is not an actionable instruction and the 8.x train must be referenced per-package. The 8.2.251219 transitive closure is SettingsControls -> Triggers -> Helpers -> Extensions -> CommunityToolkit.Common 8.2.1, all owned by Microsoft.Toolkit.
